page.overview:
What is Brave?

Brave is Pixar's thirteenth animated feature film. The film is co-written by Brenda Chapman and directed by both Chapman and Mark Andrews. It is produced by Katherine Sarafian. The score is composed by Patrick Doyle. The film was released in theaters and 3D on June 22, 2012. It was the first Pixar film animated with a new proprietary system named [https://www.pixar.com/our-story-pixar Presto].

Brave is set in ancient times in the Scottish kingdom of DunBroch and focuses on a feisty princess named Merida, the daughter of King Fergus and Queen Elinor. When Queen Elinor tells her sixteen-year-old daughter that she must marry one of the Lords' sons, a desperate Princess Merida visits a Witch who gives her a spell that will change Queen Elinor's mind. However, she ends up getting more than she bargained for. Troubles then arise when Queen Elinor succumbs to a beastly curse and transform into a black bear.

The storyline begins in the Scottish kingdom of DunBroch, with King Fergus presenting his young daughter, Merida, with a bow and arrow for her birthday, to the discomfort of Princess Merida's mother, Queen Elinor. During their outing, a giant bear named Mor'du attacks the family. Fergus fights off the bear to give Elinor and Merida a chance to escape, at the cost of his left leg.

Years later, Elinor, who has since given birth to identical triplet boys, attempts to teach Merida in the ways of the court. The princess, however, is determined to practice her archery and explore the kingdom on her horse, Angus, in what her mother calls an unladylike fashion.
